newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL rations no pipeline space for March.
newsitem.headline: IPL rations no pipeline space for March.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc unit Interprovincial Pipe Line said on Monday that requests to move oil, gas liquids and refined products on its system in March fell below capacity and no rationing of space was needed on any pipelines.

"There will be zero, or no, apportionment on all lines due to a decrease in nominations. There is, in fact, space available for all commodities for the month of March," IPL said in a message to its shippers.
Apportionment, or the amount of oil expected to move on the system subtracted from shipper nominations, was set at two percent on each of Lines 2, 3 and 13 in February.
The lines carry light, medium, heavy and synthetic crude oil to the U.S. Midwest from Western Canada.
Line 1, which moves gas liquids and refined products was also set at zero percent for February.
"IPL is able to receive nominations for extra volumes of all types," the company said.
In past years, nominations to ship crudes on IPL have skyrocked in April, May and June when refineries gear up for summer gasoline and asphalt production.
However, an expansion of the IPL system into the U.S. as well as the new 170,000 barrel per day Express Pipeline to Wyoming from Alberta were both slated to be in full operation this spring.
